open_points.subject: advance_run failure derivation for oversized mapped outputs
open_points.text: failed means a function element whose NodeExecution status is contract_violation, sandbox_violation, timeout, resource_exhausted or crashed, and an operation element that operation_element_conclusion answers ElementFailed, whatever that conclusion's status (operation_refused, operation_failed, or outcome_unknown for applied_outputs_unknown);
open_points.other_text: when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is;
open_points.question: Must the definition of failed include an oversized mapped-node aggregate with no failing element record, or must that aggregate no longer make the node failed?

open_points.subject: advance_run terminal derivation for oversized mapped outputs
open_points.text: failed means a function element whose NodeExecution status is contract_violation, sandbox_violation, timeout, resource_exhausted or crashed, and an operation element that operation_element_conclusion answers ElementFailed, whatever that conclusion's status (operation_refused, operation_failed, or outcome_unknown for applied_outputs_unknown);
open_points.other_text: a mapped node whose delivered value list is over the stored value ceiling counting as failed by the same derivation, with no record of its own,
open_points.question: How can the mapped node count as failed by this derivation when it has no NodeExecution or ElementFailed record, or which passage must change?
